newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi lists on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi lists on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange said on Wednesday that it has approved a request by Banque Audi to list its shares -- the second Lebanese commercial bank to list on the market in little over two weeks.

"The Beirut bourse committee has accepted on January 9, 1997 the listing of Banque Audi's C shares in the bourse's official market. Trading will start as of January 20, 1997," the exchange said in a statement.

The exchange said no price had not yet been set for Banque Audi's shares. Ten issues by six companies are currently trading on the stock market which reopened last year after a 13-year shutdown during the 1975-90 civil war.
Under a law passed last year, Lebanese banks can list 30 percent of their shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange and trading can begin without prior permission from the central bank.
The bank launched a heavily oversubscribed $100 million Eurobond in October lead-managed by Merrill Lynch International.

At least one other leading Beirut bank, Banque Byblos, is expected to list its shares soon on the Beriut Stock exchange. Dealers have said they expected the bank listings to invigorate trading which has been lacklustre since the market reopened.
